body:
## What to build

Preserve the contextual-share dependency rules when a summary removes an expression-local binding inside a nested evaluated expression and then reads the same name again. A removed lexical binding must not continue to hide a read of an earlier summary alias.

On main snapshot `4c63bb917ed7ed31ff6aadf060a5eae7a32cd004`, use two rows with grouping values a and b, measure x equal to one and three, and input payload prior equal to 100 and 300. Define value as the sum of x and prior as its Total share. In a later ordinary summary, assign a temporary zero to prior, pass removal of that local binding through identity, then sum prior. The call is accepted and returns derived values 100, 300 and 400, even though the displayed prior contains shares one-quarter, three-quarters and one. The documented dependency rule requires a Package condition. In the opposite direction, removing the local binding exposes an earlier ordinary alias to an otherwise eligible share source, and that forbidden source is also accepted.

Both Parent and Total shares reproduced eight nested removal spellings, including conditional, evaluated-language, argument and loop bodies, plus removal of a loop index and function formal: 38 missing refusals. Nine controls passed, including recognized straight-line removals, retained lexical bindings, a removal in a constant-false branch, and an ordinary summary without a share.

Closed #130 established conservative dependency analysis with lexical shadowing, and #162 covered non-function binding constructs. The remaining boundary is propagation of a nested removal's scope effects to later expressions, rather than introduction of a lexical scope. It is independent of computed-pronoun targets in #1021 and of external lookup-environment classification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reject the demonstrated source-to-earlier-ordinary-alias and later-ordinary-to-earlier-share dependencies with the intended Package condition.
- [ ] Cover Parent and Total helpers, nested rm/remove calls, evaluated language, argument and conditional bodies, and loop indices and function formals removed inside their bodies.
- [ ] Preserve successful independent expressions whose lexical binding remains in scope, including the demonstrated constant-false removal control.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary sequential alias evaluation when contextual shares are absent, without executing arbitrary caller expressions during analysis.
- [ ] Add public-interface regressions, preserve lazy construction and caller data, and pass the Package-affecting Review-ready check.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[Dated investigation, minimized calls and executable replay evidence](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/4e8af475cc9bc2250f105bd575706857d7960c23/investigation/2026-10-29-summary-spec-share-exhaustive/share/README.md#s1-nested-removal-preserved-a-binding-that-no-longer-existed). Recorded in PR #1055; that pull request contains investigation material only.
title: [P2] Track removed lexical bindings through nested summary expressions
